solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fruit satisfied in fall

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit
met, as in a need met or demands met

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit, its needs met, drops from the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge steeply downward is to drop, so the verb for a sharp drop matches the verb fall.

clue.text: Mischievous child cuts leg off its first unit

indicators.note: a picture instruction: rub out the slanting leg of the capital letter at the front, and what remains looks like the next letter of the alphabet but one before it

parts.note: a rascal is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A naughty child injures the leg of the first member of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: A visual trick: write a capital R and erase its diagonal leg, and a P is left, so RASCAL becomes the unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of pressure, one newton per square metre, is named after Blaise Pascal: a unit of measurement.

clue.text: One sacked after university abandons resistance

indicators.note: after places the word for sacked behind the university word

parts.note: uni is the informal word for university

indicators.note: the word for sacked abandons, or loses, the resistance symbol

parts.note: fired means sacked from a job
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A lecturer loses their job at a university and gives up the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like a number to supply letters; it is the definition, as in made one.
explanation.definitionFit: Things brought together into a single whole have become one, a united entity.

clue.text: Graduate severe about one current leading teacher

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate

indicators.note: about means the word for severe goes round the numeral one

parts.note: harsh means severe
I is the Roman numeral one
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A strict graduate deals with one modern head teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' is the physics symbol I. Maharishi Mahesh Yogi was the Beatles' guru.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu sage or spiritual guru of great standing is a leading teacher of meditation.

clue.text: Pack's expelled a communist

indicators.note: the a is expelled from the word for the card pack

parts.note: a tarot is a pack of fortune-telling cards

explanation.surface: A wolf pack has thrown out one of its members, a red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' suggests a group of animals, but it is a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Trotsky, an informal short name for that kind of communist, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Place to set free American skunk

indicators.note: letters set free from their order are let loose to rearrange, so the two words are reworked

explanation.surface: A spot where an American skunk can be released into the wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set free' is the anagram signal: the letters of PLACE TO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America the striped skunk is commonly called by the name of the European mustelid relative, a regional usage.

clue.text: Original clock face has proper gold on it

indicators.note: on it places the other pieces above the clock face in this down entry

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper
or is gold in heraldry
a dial is the face of a clock

explanation.surface: An antique clock with a gold-decorated face.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'on it' means placed above, so the proper and gold pieces sit before the clock face.
explanation.definitionFit: Existing from the very beginning of time, first in order, is the sense of original as earliest.

clue.text: Organ adds energy for fast movement

parts.note: a lung is a breathing organ
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A body part gains vigour to move quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden forward thrust of the body, as in fencing, is a quick movement.

clue.text: Cut wood, framing picture in deal successfully

indicators.note: framing means the word for coping goes round the short picture word

parts.note: to cope is to deal successfully with something
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: Cutting wood to frame a picture, and doing it well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut wood' is the definition, not an instruction: a coppice is woodland cut back regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodland regularly trimmed back to the stumps for regrowth is cut wood, a managed thicket.

clue.text: Most fine chicks could be at risk in this?

definitions.meaning: the most slender or narrow, superlative of fine

definitions.text: chicks could be at risk in this?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a nest lacking bulk, where baby birds might fall

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into THIN NEST, a sparse nest that endangers chicks.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine thread is slender, so the superlative of slim matches the superlative of fine.

clue.text: Forgers concerned with one article in museum

parts.note: smiths work metal at a forge, so they are forgers in the blacksmith sense
on, as in a talk on a subject
I is the Roman numeral one
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Counterfeiters with an interest in one item held in a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgers' suggests fakers, but here it means metalworkers at a forge. The Smithsonian Institution is a group of museums in Washington DC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Smithsonian in Washington is a famous national museum and research institution, an example of the category.

clue.text: Letter recently ignored in stamp collecting

indicators.note: the word for recently is ignored, so it is dropped from the hobby's name

parts.note: philately is the hobby of collecting postage stamps
lately means recently

explanation.surface: A letter overlooked by a stamp collector in recent times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes LATELY from PHILATELY, leaving the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the twenty-first character of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter.

clue.text: Mass of eggs, but not the first year in bird sanctuary

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for fish eggs is left off

parts.note: caviar is a mass of sturgeon roe, fish eggs

explanation.surface: Eggs laid somewhere other than the first year in a bird reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not the first' drops the C of CAVIAR, leaving AVIAR, then Y is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A large enclosure for keeping birds gives them a protected home, a loose sense of a refuge for birds.

clue.text: Comic show needs help over name

parts.note: to show up is to come, to arrive

indicators.note: over signals the word for help is turned back to front

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A comedy show needs assistance with its title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is the verb, as in turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a comic is a person who tells jokes on stage, a funny entertainer.

clue.text: Chap, though elderly, plays regularly in several ways

parts.note: a chap is a man
if can mean though, as in pleasant if dull
old means elderly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word plays

explanation.surface: An old man still plays sport regularly, in various ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks L and Y, the second and fourth letters of PLAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in many forms or many times over, a multiple manner, which is several ways.

clue.text: Father rows with son about celebrity's wicked cruelty

indicators.note: about means the father, rows and son go around the celebrity

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
a star is a celebrity
lines are rows, of seats or text

explanation.surface: A dad squabbles with his son over a famous person's nasty behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps father, rows and son around the celebrity, who lands after the first two letters. 'rows' looks like arguments but means lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cowardly, villainous and malicious is a state of wicked cruelty, so the noun names that quality.

clue.text: Inject copper into deformed toenail

indicators.note: into puts the copper symbol inside the rearranged letters
deformed means the letters of the toe word are bent out of shape

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A doctor injects copper into a misshapen toenail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deformed' rearranges the toe word to INOLATE, and 'into' puts copper's symbol after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaccinate is to inject a vaccine, so the medical verb fits inject.

clue.text: Annoying train, it runs irregularly

indicators.note: irregularly means the letters run in a disordered fashion and are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A grumble about an annoying train that runs off timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregularly' rearranges TRAIN, IT and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A source of irritation is annoying; the noun is used as an adjective meaning causing annoyance.

clue.text: Making accusations about mostly unlawful politician

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: mostly means the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: criminal means unlawful
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Accusing a politician of something that is close to illegal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the word for unlawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Recriminations are counter-charges, so the adjective describes someone making accusations in return.

clue.text: Company scheme limits one crew member

indicators.note: limits means the scheme word encloses the numeral

parts.note: a plot is a scheme
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A company plan caps the number of people on a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits' means the scheme word goes around the numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: The second pilot on an aircraft flight deck is one of the aircrew, a member of the crew.

clue.text: What a jerk's doing never rising before monarch?

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means the word is read upwards

parts.note: nay means no or never
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A fool never stands up before the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses NAY to YAN in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerk is a sharp tug, so pulling hard and suddenly is what one does; 'jerk' looks like an insult.

clue.text: One not allowing large headline

definitions.meaning: someone who bans or forbids things
a headline running the full width of a newspaper page

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a coined noun: someone who bans.
explanation.definitionFit: A full-width newspaper headline is called a banner headline, and a person who prohibits is one who bans.

clue.text: I'm after gold that's fake

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone admits chasing gold, which turns out to be counterfeit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a placing instruction, but it is the letters POST.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a fake can be a person who pretends to be someone else, a pretender or fraud.

clue.text: Small bag for art

parts.note: a hunter's bag is the game killed, the kill

explanation.surface: A small bag made for art supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter's 'bag' is the total of game shot, the kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Art in the sense of craft or knack, as in the art of persuasion, is ability or expertise.

clue.text: Only partially sanguine about money

indicators.note: Only partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is only half optimistic about their finances.
explanation.walkthrough: A guinea was an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings, still used in pricing horses.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a former British coin and sum of money, an example of currency.

clue.text: Old were furious when right's lost

indicators.note: lost means the right letter goes missing from the word for were furious

parts.note: raged means were furious
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Old people were angry when their rights were taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes R from RAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: Having lived many years means being elderly, a direct synonym of old.

clue.text: There's a point to this law needing reform

indicators.note: a law needing reform must be re-formed, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A campaigner argues there is a purpose to changing a faulty law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing reform' is the anagram signal on LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed tool for punching holes in leather has a sharp tip, so it is a thing with a point.

clue.text: Popular — till people will show resentment

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
to till soil is to dig it
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A popular cash register prompts public anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till' looks like a cash register or 'until', but it is the verb for working soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger at unfair treatment is resentment, a close synonym.

clue.text: Completely or nearly closed account

parts.note: a door pushed to is nearly shut
a tally is a running account or reckoning

explanation.surface: A bank account that is completely, or almost, closed.
explanation.walkthrough: A door that is 'to' is pulled almost shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean entirely, wholly, without exception: plain synonyms.

clue.text: Note port light on front of German boat

indicators.note: on front of places the first two pieces ahead of the abbreviation for German

parts.note: D is a musical note
the light on a ship's port side is red

explanation.surface: A note about a ship's port light on the bow of a German vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ships carry a red light on the port (left) side and green on starboard.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a vessel that scoops mud from the bottom of a channel, so it is a type of boat.
